interest: Grew notes suits against Japan's government were rare in practice, despite statutory equality, in a 1938 reciprocity inquiry.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.0433/1 through 894.0433/5, dating from September 8, 1938 to September 19, 1939) documents an official inquiry initiated by Washington attorney Charles E. Foster, Jr. regarding whether American citizens have the right to prosecute claims against the Government of Japan in its national courts. Foster, representing a Japanese national with a claim against the United States, required proof of reciprocal legal access under Section 261 of Title 28 of the United States Code (36 Stat. 1139) to establish jurisdiction in the U.S. Court of Claims. In response, the Department of State instructed U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo to obtain an official statement from the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Japanese Foreign Office confirmed that under the Japanese Code of Civil Procedure and Imperial Ordinance No. 3 of 1891, the Imperial Government occupied a coordinate position with subjects in civil cases, public law matters were litigated in separate administrative courts, criminal proceedings could not be brought against the State, and American citizens enjoyed equal legal standing with Japanese subjects. Ambassador Grew supplemented this with an analytical despatch noting the practical limitations imposed by Japan's Roman-law administrative courts. The State Department forwarded these diplomatic notes and statutory translations to Foster in October 1938, and subsequently transmitted copies to Attorney General Frank Murphy and the Department of Justice in September 1939 for use in the pending litigation.

subfiles.about: Attorney Charles E. Foster, Jr. requests that the Department of State ascertain whether American citizens can sue the Government of Japan in its national courts to establish reciprocity for a suit in the U.S. Court of Claims.
subfiles.summary: Charles E. Foster, Jr. asks State whether Americans can sue the Japanese Government, needed for a Japanese client's Court of Claims suit.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles E. Foster, Jr. to Secretary of State Requesting Information on Suits Against Japanese Government
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (Attention: William R. Vallance)

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs the American Embassy in Tokyo by telegraph to obtain an official statement from the Japanese Foreign Office on whether American citizens may sue the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: Billing copy of a telegram asking the Tokyo embassy what suits Americans may bring against the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Department of State to American Embassy in Tokyo (Division of Accounts Copy)

subfiles.about: Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth notifies Charles E. Foster, Jr. that an instruction has been telegraphed to the American Ambassador at Tokyo at Foster's expense.
subfiles.summary: Green H. Hackworth tells Charles E. Foster, Jr. that Tokyo has been asked by telegraph, at his expense, whether Americans can sue Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth to Charles E. Foster, Jr.

subfiles.about: William R. Vallance details his discussions with Charles E. Foster, Jr. and notes that the inquiry to Tokyo follows a 1921 precedent established during Joseph C. Grew's mission in Copenhagen.
subfiles.summary: William R. Vallance reports arranging, at Foster's expense, a cable to Tokyo on suing the Japanese Government, modeled on a 1921 instruction.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from William R. Vallance to Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs the American Embassy in Tokyo to obtain an official statement from the Japanese Foreign Office on the standing of American citizens to sue the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Tokyo embassy for a Foreign Office statement on whether Americans can sue the Japanese Government, for a Court of Claims case.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Department of State to American Embassy in Tokyo (File Copy)

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew telegraphs the Japanese Foreign Office's preliminary reply confirming that the Japanese Government occupies a coordinate position with subjects in civil suits.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Foreign Office says the Japanese Government stands equal to private parties in civil cases, and Americans may sue on the same basis.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 627 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth transmits the telegraphic report from Tokyo regarding civil suits against the Japanese Government to Charles E. Foster, Jr.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth relays to Foster Grew's report that Americans may sue the Japanese Government in civil cases on equal terms with Japanese subjects.
subfiles.title: Letter from Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth to Charles E. Foster, Jr.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits copies and translations of diplomatic correspondence and statutes, commenting on the practical limitations of suits against Japan under Roman administrative law.
subfiles.summary: Grew's Despatch No. 3304 forwards the Foreign Office notes and statutes, observing that suits against the Japanese Government are few in practice.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3304 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The American Embassy in Tokyo presents three formal questions to the Japanese Foreign Office regarding the right of aliens to sue the Japanese Government in its courts.
subfiles.summary: Embassy Note No. 1046 asks the Foreign Office what suits may be brought against the Japanese Government and whether Americans may bring them equally.
subfiles.title: Note Verbale No. 1046 from American Embassy in Tokyo to Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirms the coordinate standing of the State and private litigants in civil cases and affirms equal standing for American citizens.
subfiles.summary: Foreign Office Note No. 88 says the Japanese Government stands equal with subjects in civil cases, cannot be charged criminally, and Americans may sue equally.
subfiles.title: Note Verbale No. 88/Treaty II from Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs to American Embassy in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Translations of Article 4 of the Japanese Code of Civil Procedure and Imperial Ordinance No. 3 of 1891 defining jurisdiction and representation in civil suits against the State.
subfiles.from: Imperial Japanese Government (translated by American Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Translations of Article 4 of Japan's Code of Civil Procedure and Imperial Ordinance No. 3 of 1891 on State representation in civil suits.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Translations of Japanese Code of Civil Procedure (Article 4) and Imperial Ordinance No. 3 of 1891
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Tokyo / Department of State

subfiles.about: Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth transmits copies of Ambassador Grew's despatch, diplomatic notes, and translations of Japanese statutes to Charles E. Foster, Jr.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth sends Charles E. Foster, Jr. Grew's Despatch No. 3304 with the Japanese notes and law translations, for alleging reciprocity in the Court of Claims.
subfiles.title: Letter from Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth to Charles E. Foster, Jr. Transmitting Translations

subfiles.about: Counselor R. Walton Moore transmits Ambassador Grew's despatch and statutory translations regarding suits against Japan to Attorney General Frank Murphy.
subfiles.summary: R. Walton Moore sends Attorney General Frank Murphy Grew's Despatch No. 3304 on suits against the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Letter from Counselor R. Walton Moore to Attorney General Frank Murphy

subfiles.about: Assistant Attorney General Francis M. Shea acknowledges receipt of the State Department's transmittal of Ambassador Grew's despatch and enclosures regarding suits against Japan.
subfiles.summary: Francis M. Shea acknowledges Moore's September 18, 1939 letter enclosing Grew's despatch on suits against the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Attorney General Francis M. Shea to Counselor R. Walton Moore
